gaps: The close path has no specified way to derive the promised full-diff list. `_measure` excludes `.factory/`, `plans/` and decisions, and compares against effective scope, which includes amendments; the existing review brief lists only recorded amendments. The plan must name a separate stage-base diff calculation that retains excluded paths and identifies strays against declared scope (factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:1553, factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:1573, factory/scripts/forge_cli/review_brief.py:432).

Listing changed records, plans and decisions by name does not let the reviewer judge their contents: the detached review tip restores excluded paths to the base before Autoreview reads its diff. The plan does not say how those changes become reviewable while preserving the existing review boundary (factory/scripts/forge_cli/review.py:1262, factory/scripts/forge_cli/review.py:1283).

The proposed PR-body update must run when a PR is already open. `seal_task` currently returns immediately after finding that PR, so merely adding `gh pr edit` to the create path would leave rerun updates unreachable; the plan also leaves the absent-block case and edit-failure behavior unstated (factory/scripts/forge_cli/tasks.py:725, factory/scripts/forge_cli/tasks.py:737).

The Lite change needs a review and budget path independent of product filtering. Today Lite review drops excluded prefixes and rewrites them out of the detached review tip, while `mode done` counts only paths classified as product. A window changing only a previously exempt committed file cannot meet the stated 'every committed change' criterion through those paths (factory/scripts/forge_cli/review.py:2013, factory/scripts/forge_cli/review.py:2055, factory/scripts/forge_cli/quickfix.py:312, factory/scripts/forge_cli/quickfix.py:435).

Deleting `docs/degraded-mode.md` leaves upgraded clients with their old copy: upgrade copies documents only when the source exists and has no retirement operation for this path. The plan needs an explicit upgrade disposition for that formerly shipped guide, including a client copy that has diverged (factory/scripts/forge_cli/scaffold.py:46, factory/scripts/forge_cli/upgrade.py:4773).

The documentation sweep misses executable guidance that will still direct people to removed routes: `forge next` recommends quickfix and hook-blocked writes, signal guidance points to the deleted degraded guide, and generated onboarding text recommends a five-file quickfix. These need named replacements in the task scope (factory/scripts/forge_cli/phase.py:503, factory/scripts/forge_cli/signal.py:76, factory/scripts/forge_cli/scaffold.py:225).

Marking `strict-role-split.md` superseded would break at least one existing linked story: `plan save` resolves its roadmap spec with `confirmed=True`, and that resolver accepts only `status: confirmed`. The plan says existing links stay valid but specifies only skipping superseded specs for new links; it needs a historical-link rule at the existing-link consumer (plans/roadmap.json:561, factory/scripts/forge_cli/plans.py:301, factory/scripts/forge_cli/specs.py:96).

The proof section says only 'add tests for each acceptance criterion' and 'fix the Windows CI selector.' It leaves the executable integration checks and exact selectors to guess, including the no-launch close, PR-block rerun, retained command denials, full Lite review, legacy records, and the Windows job's multiple lockout and degraded selectors (docs/specs/full-access.md:84, .github/workflows/factory-scaffold.yml:119, .github/workflows/factory-scaffold.yml:141).
contradictions: REMOVE-LOCK and CLOSE-JUDGES are proposed as parallel tasks with disjoint scopes, but both explicitly require changes to `quickfix.py`: the former removes write-time claims and the repo-kind pin, while the latter changes Lite counting and removes degraded and quickfix commands. They cannot run as the stated disjoint-scope parallel pair (factory/scripts/forge_cli/quickfix.py:94, factory/scripts/forge_cli/quickfix.py:163, factory/scripts/forge_cli/quickfix.py:284).
resolutions: Close computes a separate stage-base diff (committed base..HEAD plus working tree, all paths) against the DECLARED write scope to list strays and overlaps (Technical approach: Close).
The review brief carries the text diff of changed plans/ and docs/decisions/ files so Autoreview can judge their content; .factory/ records are listed by name (Technical approach: Close).

seal_task updates the marked Forge block both on create and when a PR already exists (replace or append, gh pr edit); an edit failure warns with the retry command and does not fail the close (Technical approach: PR body).
Lite budget and review use the full committed diff since the window base with no product filtering; the review tip keeps every changed path (Technical approach: Lite).
Client copies of docs/degraded-mode.md are retired by FORGE-UPG-2's byte-ownership rule: byte-equal copies removed, edited copies kept (Technical approach: Degraded and quickfix).

Guidance pointing at removed routes is reworded to the Lite fix: phase.py quickfix and hook-blocked-write advice, signal.py's degraded-guide pointer, and scaffolded onboarding text, in CLOSE-JUDGES' scope (Technical approach).
The spec resolver accepts confirmed or superseded specs for existing roadmap links (plan save, sign-off) and only confirmed specs for new links (Technical approach: Specs).
Tests are named per acceptance item in factory/tests/test_full_access.py, and the Windows job's exact selectors to drop, reduce and add are listed (Technical approach: Tests).

All quickfix.py changes (including claim_files and the repo-kind pin) move to CLOSE-JUDGES; REMOVE-LOCK owns the hook, worker_admission, repo_kind, delegate write admission and hook wiring, so the two task scopes are disjoint and parallel (Technical approach: Tasks).

## Task decomposition

CODE first, then DOCS. Each ships its own pull request.

| Label / exact task ID | What it delivers | Depends on | user_facing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Code / CODE | Write guard, write admission and revocation deleted; hook wiring and its checks (presence and absence); retained command gates kept; launch-free close with stray, overlap and records lists; PR block; stage-bound amendments; full Lite review and budget; degraded and quickfix removed; superseded-spec link rule; reworded guidance | none | false |
| Docs / DOCS | Canon, skill, brief and session-start wording; `docs/degraded-mode.md` deleted; `strict-role-split.md` superseded | CODE | false |

## Verify plan

Each task: focused tests in `factory/tests/test_full_access.py`, `forge task close` (full suite plus
one three-lens review), the CI-only checks, and green CI including the Windows hook job with its
updated selectors. The story is done when a real coordinator session edits product, canon and
`.factory` files without a refusal, a task with an out-of-scope file closes with that file listed in
its review brief and PR block, and destructive commands and raw `codex exec` are still refused.
